item.title: Being You - A New Science of Consciousness
item.description:
Things that question being/consciousness

  • What does anaesthesia do to your consciousness? Where does the state of being temporarily get abolished to?
  • Where does subjective universe come into play?

Real problem of consciousness

Explain, predict, and control the phenomenological properties of conscious experience. It’s different from hard problem because it’s not trying to place consciousness in relation to the universe. It doesn’t need a magic like property for consciousness.

Historical Ideas

Study of consciousness and trying to know it almost feels impossible, but we felt the same about phenomenon of being alive quiet some time ago. Theories like vitalism tried explaining it similarly to how dualism tried explaining consciousness. With modern medical science, we came to understand what being alive meant. So, there is a good argument that we will figure the consciousness part as well. The only major hurdle is being alive is objective but consciousness is subjective.

item.title: Quiet - The power of introverts in a world that can't stop talking
item.description:
• Introverts focus on the Meaning they make of the events swirling around them; extroverts plunge into the events themselves.
  • Introverts recharge their batteries by being alone; extroverts need to recharge when they don’t socialize enough.
  • Introverts are mostly slow and deliberate. So, there is a chance that they’re immune to the lures of wealth and fame.
  • Introverts, may have strong skills and enjoy business parties and meetings, but after a while wish they were home in their pajamas. Most have a horror of small talk, but enjoy deep discussions.
  • Shyness is inherently painful; introversion is not. People often overlap these two concepts.
  • The more a person talks, the more other group members direct their attention to that person, which means that he becomes increasingly powerful as the meeting goes on. It also helps to speak fast; we rate quick talkers as more capable and appealing than slow talkers. But, there’s no such link between more talking and greater insight.
  • “Bus to Abilene” anecdote reveals our tendency to follow those who initiate action - any action. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abilene_paradox People decide on a course of action that is counter to preferences of many or all individuals in the group.
  • Interesting findings:
    • More Creative people tend to be socially poised introverts. They described themselves as and individualistic.
    • Solitude can be a catalyst to innovation.
      • Only when you are alone, you can engage in deliberate practice.
      • Deliberate practice takes intense concentration. It requires deep motivation, often self-generated. It involves working on the task that’s most challenging to us personally.
    • Open Plan offices have been found to reduce productivity and impair memory.
    • Simple act of being interrupted is one of the biggest barriers of Productivity among knowledge workers.
    • Multitasking is a myth.
    • Group work is not as people point it out to be. Rather than creativity, social glue is the principal benefit from these sessions.

“Evidence from science suggests that business people must be insane to use brainstorming groups. If you have talented and motivated people, they should be encouraged to work alone when creativity or efficiency is the highest priority.” – Adrian Furnham

Notes

  • None of us live in an objective world, but instead in a subjective world that we ourselves have given meaning to. The world you see is different from the one I see, and it’s impossible to share your world with anyone else.
  • If environments condition people, all those who had bad parents must turn the same way.
  • “Past doesn’t matter.” according to Alderian Psychology.
  • Teleology: Study of purpose of a given phenomenon rather than study of causation (etiology). Your friend had the goal of not going out beforehand, and he’s been manufacturing a state of anxiety and fear as a means to achieve that goal.
  • We make out of trauma whatever suits our purposes. Experiences don’t determine but the meaning we give them is self-determining.
  • Immediate rewards for people: e.g. He is creating anxiety and fear as his reasons to stay inside. It’s not that the person is happy or satisfied but there’s no doubt that person is acting in alignment to his/her goal.
  • People get angry that they could shout.
  • People anticipate things that the other person will say, the measures they will take to correct their mistake and humble apology. But, people want to shout and they shout. This is way you show your power over others. You used emotion of anger as tool to make the other person submit to you.
  • Mother, principal, call, anger as a choice, anger to overpower child with loud voice thus assert her opinions.
  • People have emotions but they have control over it.
  • If past would only determine everyone’s future, we would end up with nihilism and pessimism losing any hope.
  • People think their disposition or personality cannot be changed. In Adlerian psychology, we describe personality and disposition with the word “lifestyle." Lifestyle is a word that encompasses the worldview of that person and his or her outlook on life.
  • Example of How personality can be reformed: Say there’s someone who worries about himself and says, “I am a pessimist.” One could rephrase that to instead say, “I have a pessimistic view of the world.” You could consider that the issue is not personality but rather the view of the world. It seems that the word “personality” is nuanced and suggests being unchangeable. But if we’re talking about a view of the world, well, then, that should be possible to alter.
  • You probably think that lifestyle you have is the most practical one and it’s easier to leave things as they are.
  • Changing lifestyle needs courage. Anxiety generated by changing vs Disappointment of not changing. Most people go for the latter.

Objectives of human behavior and psychology

  • For behavior: a. Be self reliant b. Live in harmony with society
  • For psychology that supports these behaviors: a. I have the ability. b. The consciousness that people are my comrades.

    • Tasks of work
      • No choice but to confront when to live as a social being.
      • Work cannot be completed all by oneself.
      • Interpersonal relationships of work are lowest bar hurdles because of clear objective of getting good results. So, people work together even if they don’t always get along.
      • Persons tripped up in this stage are “NEETs”: young person not in education, training or employment / shut-ins (person confined indoors).
    • Tasks of friendship
    • Tasks of Love
      • Relationships in which people restrict each other eventually fall apart.
      • One should not have feeling of inferiority or need of boasting when with the person they love.

        • Love relationships : Connected by a red string
        • Relationships with family (particularly parent-child relation): Connected by rigid chains

Goal of interpersonal relationships: Community Feeling

  • Seeing other people as our comrades
  • Community is not just household, school, workplace, society or even nations and humanity but entire axis of time from past to the future, all plants, animals and even inanimate objects.
  • People who are obsessed with a desire for recognition will seem to be looking at other people while they are actually looking only at themselves.
  • “I” is the protagonist in one’s life. But “I” doesn’t rule the center of the world. “I” is never more than a member of community and part of a whole.
  • People obsessed with themselves, for them others means only those “who will do something” for them.
  • In Alderian psychology, sense of belonging is something that can be attained by making active commitment to community of one’s own accord, not by being here.
  • Rather than what will the person give me ? What can I give to this person? This is commitment to the community.
  • It’s natural that when we search for a sense of belonging, we will be attracted to the smaller community.
  • We search for sense of belonging here and there. Rather than not finding your sense of belonging and shrinking to smaller fo of community such as from school to shutting yourself to home, you can find you belong elsewhere if you see whole world is for you to belong.
  • When you run into difficulties with interpersonal relations and no longer see a way out, “Listen to the voice of the larger community.”
  • Living in fear of one’s relationships falling apart is an unfree way to live, in which one is living for other people.

Horizontal Relationships

  • A relation of equals. You don’t seem to be above or below someone else.
  • A parent also must not make a child feel that he/she is in a vertical relationship.
  • In child rearing, one must not praise. Physical punishment, rebuking is out of the course obviously. By praising “passing of judgment by a person of ability to a person of no ability”, it’s taking place. e.g. Mother says to a child helping her “You are a good helper.” but not to her husband. This is unconsciously creating hierarchical relationships and seeing child as beneath her.
  • Whether we praise or rebuke, background goal is manipulation. Reward-punishment education’s intention is to manipulate children.
  • All relationships should be horizontal as per Alderian psychology.
  • If one can build horizontal relationships “equal but not the same” for all people, there is no room for inferiority complexes to emerge.
  • People intervene because of vertical relationships.
  • Assistance and intervention are two different things. Assistance presupposes separation of tasks and horizontal relationships.
  • If one is not following through one’s own tasks, it’s not because of ability but because of lack of courage to face one’s tasks. So, all we do is give them courage to work on their task.
  • The more one is praised by another person, the more one forms the belief that one has no ability.
  • The most important thing is to not judge other people. “Judgment” is a word that comes out of vertical relationships. If one is building horizontal relationships, there will be words of more straightforward gratitude and respect and joy.
  • The goal is to be able to say “I can make contributions to other people”.
  • Context matters the most. If your life were in danger, and you were hanging on by a thread, the people around you would probably feel very gladdened just by the very fact of your existing. They would simply feel thankful that you are safe in the here and now, and would not be wanting you to perform some direct act.
  • People have ideal disposition and subtract scores from that ideal to judge a person. Instead of taking points away from ideal image, people could start from zero. Then, the mere existence is grateful.
  • If you are building even one vertical relationship with someone, you will be treating all your interpersonal relationships as vertical.
  • Even if you are not treating them in a boss-or-subordinate kind of way, it is as if you are saying, “A is above me, and B is below me,” for example, or “I’ll follow A’s advice, but ignore what B says,” or “I don’t mind breaking my promise to C.” This is what happens.
  • People have a space to refuse and a space to propose better way of doing things. We feel there is no space for all of it so that we can avoid conflict and responsibility.
  • There is no need to go out of one’s way to be positive and affirm oneself. It’s not self-affirmation that we are concerned with, but self-acceptance.
  • Switch from attachment to self –> concern for others requires three things:
    • Self-acceptance
      • Self-affirmation is making suggestions to oneself when something is beyond one’s ability. It can bring superiority complex. Self-acceptance is accepting a person’s incapable self and moving forward to do best that can be done.
    • Confidence in others
      • Trust vs Confidence: Trust comes with set conditions. We refer to it as credit. Bank borrows you money based on trust that you can pay back this much of money. Confidence is doing without any set conditions whatsoever when believing in others. Even if someone doesn’t have objective grounds for trust, one believes.
      • In Alderian psychology, basis of interpersonal relationships is founded not on trust but on confidence.
      • In times, people who believe unconditionally gets taken advantage of. The attitude of continuing to believe in someone even in such instances is what we call confidence.
      • Believing unconditionally doesn’t have moral significance here. It’s to make interpersonal relationship with the person better and build a horizontal relationship.
      • Don’t just focus on the wounds that people give by believing in them. In long run, you will have many deep relationships if you try this.
      • Courage to overcome fear of being taken advantage of comes from self-acceptance. If you see as taking advantage is other person’s task, getting to core of confidence in others becomes less difficult.
      • Placing confidence in others is connected to seeing other people as comrades.
    • Contribution to others
      • Contribution to others doesn’t mean self-sacrifice. People who sacrifice too much are conformed to society too much.
      • e.g. If you do all the household work in a family, you normally ask yourself these questions: Why don’t they give me a hand? Why do I have to do all the work? I should have at least received a Thank You from them. If I hum like this, I am probably not much fun to be around. If I am enjoying it, someone might come and give a hand.
      • You need to be creating an atmosphere in which its easier to offer help.
  • These three go in circle. You accept yourself thereby can have confidence in others. You have confidence, you see others as comrades. Now, you can engage in contributing to others. This gives feeling of “I am of use to someone” and it helps accept oneself as one is. And the circle repeats.
  • Stammering, feeling of inferiority, become too self conscious as a result, tipping words more and more.
  • People are aware of their worth only when they feel “I am of use to someone”. One just needs a subjective sense of it. Happiness is a feeling of contribution.

One makes trouble for another person while trying at the same time to be “special.”
  • People can’t accept normal self. People want to feel special. The old way doesn’t work and they make huge leap of being especially bad - the opposite.
  • Being normal is not being incapable. One doesn’t need to flaunt superiority.
  • Life is a series of dots. It’s a series of moments what you felt like a continuous line. A series of moments called ’now’. Our lives only exist in the moments. If life were a line, life planning would be possible. Since it’s a series of dots, it’s impossible to plan next.
  • The life that lies ahead of you is a completely blank page, and there are no tracks that have been laid for you to follow. There’s no story there.
  • The greatest life lie of all is not to live here and now. Believing that you know how the line goes is the biggest lie.
  • So life in general has no meaning whatsoever. But you can assign meaning to that life. And you are the only one who can assign meaning to your life.
  • You are lost in your life. Why are you lost? You are lost because you are trying to choose freedom, that is to say, a path on which you are not afraid of being disliked by others and you are not living others’ lives—a path that is yours alone.
  • In Alderian psychology, the guiding star to happiness is “Contribution to others”
  • One more time, I give you the words of Adler: “Someone has to start. Other people might not be cooperative, but that is not connected to you. My advice is this: You should start. With no regard to whether others are cooperative or not.”

The transparency of the rigged social proof we get these days provides us with exactly the cue we need for knowing when to perform this simple maneuver. With no more cost than a bit of vigilance for plainly counterfeit social evidence, then, we can protect ourselves nicely.

  • loc 2653 - So if a pair of freeway drivers decided by coincidence to change lanes at the identical moment, the next two drivers might well do the same, assuming that the forward drivers had spotted an obstruction. The resulting social evidence confronting drivers behind this group would be potent—four successive cars, all with their turn signals flashing, trying to angle into the next lane. More signal lights would go on. The social proof would be undeniable by then.

  • loc 2659 - An automatic-pilot device, like social proof, should never be trusted fully; even when no saboteur has fed bad information into the mechanism, it can sometimes go haywire by itself. We need to check the machine from time to time to be sure that it hasn’t worked itself out of sync with the other sources of evidence in the situation—the objective facts, our prior experiences, our own judgments. Fortunately, this precaution requires neither much effort nor much time. A quick glance around is all that is needed.

  • loc 2694 - social proof is most powerful for those who feel unfamiliar or unsure in a specific situation and who, consequently, must look outside of themselves for evidence of how best to behave there.

item.title: Self-Knowledge
item.description:
Author: Mark Manson

  • loc 47 - When you did the exercise and your mind kept wandering back to what you had to do at work tomorrow, who was it that was watching your mind worry about work tomorrow? It was your mind watching your mind. In Zen they refer to this as the “Thinking Mind” and the “Observing Mind” – the two minds.

  • loc 54 - The problem with the Thinking Mind is that we don’t completely control it.

  • loc 64 - Our Thinking Mind is like a horny dog on a leash that keeps running after things and if we aren’t used to using our Observing Mind, then our Thinking Mind drags us along with it.

  • loc 75 - In Zen, they advise that instead of saying, “I am angry,” to say, “I feel anger.” Instead of saying, “I am nervous,” say, “I feel nervousness.” Instead of saying, “I am jealous,” you say, “I feel jealousy.”

  • loc 118 - “My boss is not an idiot. But I am having the thought that my boss is an idiot.” “I don’t hate my ex-girlfriend. I am feeling hatred toward my ex-girlfriend.” “I am not lonely and depressed. I am feeling loneliness and depression.” Language is very powerful. Notice when you disidentify from these emotions and thoughts in this way it 1) implies that they’re temporary states, and not permanent conditions and 2) forces you to take responsibility for them. They’re nobody’s fault, they just are.

  • loc 126 - “Thank you Thinking Mind for feeling nervous before my date tonight. It will keep me on my toes!” “Thank you Thinking Mind for being angry at my boss. I really appreciate how much you care.” This is going to feel really bizarre – expressing gratitude towards negative emotions. But I think you’ll find that it diminishes the power of the thoughts and emotions over time and actually impels you to take action despite them.

  • loc 230 - It doesn’t matter whether a belief is true or not; what matters is whether it’s helpful. Believing you are ugly, or undesirable, or not interesting enough – these may or may not be true in various circumstances. But they can never be proven one way or another. So why not assume they’re untrue? What do you have to lose?

item.title: The 48 Laws of Power
item.description:
Author: Greene, Robert

  • loc 147 - Niccolò Machiavelli wrote, “Any man who tries to be good all the time is bound to come to ruin among the great number who are not good.”

  • loc 299 - NEVER OUTSHINE THE MASTER

  • loc 300 - Always make those above you feel comfortably superior. In your desire to please and impress them, do not go too far in displaying your talents or you might accomplish the opposite—inspire fear and insecurity. Make your masters appear more brilliant than they are and you will attain the heights of power.

  • loc 327 - The evening of the party, as Fouquet presented spectacle on spectacle to Louis, each more magnificent than the one before, he imagined the affair as demonstrating his loyalty and devotion to the king.

  • loc 330 - Instead, however, each new spectacle, each appreciative smile bestowed by the guests on Fouquet, made it seem to Louis that his own friends and subjects were more charmed by the finance minister than by the king himself, and that Fouquet was actually flaunting his wealth and power.

  • loc 424 - NEVER PUT TOO MUCH TRUST IN FRIENDS, LEARN HOW TO USE ENEMIES

  • loc 425 - Be wary of friends—they will betray you more quickly, for they are easily aroused to envy. They also become spoiled and tyrannical. But hire a former enemy and he will be more loyal than a friend, because he has more to prove. In fact, you have more to fear from friends than from enemies. If you have no enemies, find a way to make them.
